name: 370 mm scale test, 3 mm gap
notes: The geometry that motivated this work: a 370 mm outer diameter with a 3 mm air gap, the proportions of a YASA-class axial-flux machine. A uniform grid needs ~54 million cells for three across that gap and 432 million for six. Meshed in cylindrical coordinates over one pole pair it is under a million. Note this is a scale test of the mesh and solver, not a model of a YASA motor: the topology is still the PCB coreless stator with a low-permeability salient-pole rotor, because permanent magnets and high-mu steel are outside what the reduced scalar potential can represent (see docs/limitations.md).
